headline: Five weeks on: 3 deaths, 4,503 homes destroyed among 22,245 evaluated, and about 2,700 people still in shelters (SINAPROC, 13 Nov). Rebuilding is scaling up, with contracts for 4,197 replacement homes, and aftershocks continue at about 20 a day.
key_points: Official (13 Nov): 3 deaths, 27 injured; of 22,245 homes evaluated, 4,503 destroyed, 10,836 moderate or partial damage.
Shelters: 91 still open, mostly in Veraguas and Los Santos; 2,731 people at last count (8 Nov).
Housing: 75 contracts for 4,197 replacement homes; Cabinet now offers a new home, a cash equivalent or a repair grant.
Health: CSS units at Remón, San Cristóbal, Los Pozos and Tonosí closed or in tents; Los Pozos sanitation critical (UN).
Water: 26 of 45 inspected IDAAN tanks critically damaged, including Chitré's main reserve; Farfán (Soná) lost its tank.
Aftershocks: 1,500+ so far, now ~20 a day; M4.8 events on 11–12 Nov felt in the capital.
Schools: year 2027 starts 1 March as planned; temporary classrooms for ~5,500 students; UNICEF/EU spaces reach 6,800+ children.

areas.area: Los Santos (Macaracas, Tonosí, Las Tablas, Pedasí)
areas.text: 1,285 replacement homes contracted, the most of any province. Tonosí: hospital and CSS unit work from tents; repair evaluations moved from Tonosí to Isla Cañas and Macaracas. Pedasí waives municipal taxes on repairs for 12 months.

areas.area: Herrera (Los Pozos, Las Minas, Pesé, Ocú, Chitré)
areas.text: Los Pozos CSS clinic works from the municipal court, and its temporary hospital has critical sanitation gaps. Chitré: main 400,000-gallon water tank out of service, polyclinic in a modular unit. Pesé public library declared unfit for use.

Most people still in shelters; 850 replacement homes contracted. Collapsed tanks and aqueducts leave Farfán and other Soná communities short of water; Santa Catalina and Mariato tourism and fishing hit hard. M4.8 aftershock south of Soná on 12 Nov.
439 replacement homes contracted; demolition of collapsed schools continues; IDAAN repairs at the Natá water plant; most shelters closed.
Mostly adobe homes damaged; about 16 of 130 homes evaluated in the comarca collapsed. Fire stations in David (central) and Gualaca to be demolished; Santa Marta (Bugaba) water plant damaged.

Policlínica Presidente Remón and ULAPS San Cristóbal still closed; CSS senior centres in San Miguelito and Plaza 5 de Mayo closed for damage. Colón: 200+ families from cracked buildings to be relocated.

services.text: 4,503 destroyed and 10,836 with moderate or partial damage (13 Nov); 4,197 replacement homes contracted; options include a new home, cash or a repair grant; replacement homes due by 31 March 2027.
853 schools evaluated; school year starts 1 March 2027; temporary learning spaces in Soná, Tonosí, Macaracas and La Villa for ~5,500 students.
CSS: Remón and San Cristóbal closed; Los Pozos and Tonosí in temporary sites; Chitré polyclinic modular; Soná and Santiago hospitals with closed areas.
All roads open and landslides almost cleared; plan to repair 16–17 bridges going to Cabinet; Búcaro work continues; Macaracas–Tonosí road to be tendered.
Most water plants restored, but 26 of 45 inspected tanks have critical damage; 19 tanker trucks in use; power largely restored.
Tocumen and Metro Lines 1 and 2 operating since 12 Oct; state ports back to ~80%.

upcoming: Coming up: Cabinet decision on MOP bridge repairs; MICI business-damage register; WFP cash assistance from early December.
unknowns: How many homes need full replacement: SINAPROC counts 4,503 destroyed; MIVIOT says 4,000–6,000.
How many repair grants will be paid, and how fast, under the new Cabinet resolution.
Where Isla Cañas residents will be relocated.
Total public cost: MOP bridge costs and private business losses are still not published.
